sections.content:
223,675 people

were counted on the census as "teaching assistants" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Teaching assistants assist teachers with their day-to-day classroom work and with routine administrative tasks.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "teaching assistants" there were more women than men (91.4% compared with 8.6%).

This means "teaching assistants" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "caring personal service occupations".

Men made up 8.6% and women made up 91.4% of "teaching assistants"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "teaching assistants" included:

  • legal secretaries
  • occupational therapists
  • receptionists

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "teaching assistants" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "teaching assistants", 15.7% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "teaching assistants" was 65 years or older.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "teaching assistants" included:

  • educational support assistants
  • vehicle body builders and repairers
  • printing machine assistants

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "teaching assistants" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "teaching assistants" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "teaching assistants", 11.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (54.1% compared with 45.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98.1%) than self-employed (1.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
